newsitem.title: JAPAN: All Tokyo corn futures end daily 400 yen limit-up.
newsitem.headline: All Tokyo corn futures end daily 400 yen limit-up.

text.p: All Tokyo corn futures ended up by the daily 400 yen limit on Tuesday on heavy buying from individual investors following the Chicago market's price gains overnight and the yen's weakness against the dollar, traders said.
The benchmark January 1998 contract was up 400 yen at 15,590 yen per tonne at the closing. Volume was 115,549 lots.

Local investors, encouraged by the firmer sentiment of the Chicago market, continued to buy from the opening, traders said. "The weaker yen motivated investors to accelerate buying in late afternoon," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot March contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.75 per bushel at 0810 GMT, unchanged from Monday's close.
The spot March of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.50 at 0810 GMT, up from $7.49-3/4 at Monday's close.
